A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Geo-ID work. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–F are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching renumbered appendix tables.

before.justification: v1 reports original consistency and decomposition experiments, runtime measurements, ablations, geometry-sensitivity analyses, and qualitative downstream results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds unordered-input Diffusion Renderer results, runtime comparisons, and quantitative downstream albedo reconstruction results.

M1.justification: The VGGT correspondence pipeline, weighted-median voxel consensus, visibility filtering, and diffusion guidance procedure remain unchanged. v2 specifies the observation-weight formula more precisely but does not establish a change to the implemented method.

E1.justification: Section 4.7 adds held-out-pose albedo novel-view synthesis as an explicitly evaluated task, extending the earlier qualitative relighting and material-editing demonstrations. InteriorVerse, HyperSim, MipNeRF-360, and Tanks&Temples coverage otherwise remains unchanged.

E2.justification: Diffusion Renderer joins the runtime comparison in Table 4. The new downstream comparison includes ordered Diffusion Renderer and both unguided base predictors. Comparator identities in the original intrinsic benchmarks are retained; splitting Diffusion Renderer into ordered and unordered settings is a protocol change.

E3.justification: v2 adds Diffusion Renderer evaluation on the same randomized subsets as Geo-ID, retaining its previous results as the ordered condition. The new downstream protocol trains MeshSplatting on subsets of predicted albedos and scores held-out renders against each method’s own predictions using PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS.

E4.justification: The ordered-versus-unordered Diffusion Renderer comparison adds an input-order sensitivity analysis. Existing component ablations, geometry-quality analyses, confidence-threshold and voxel-size sensitivity tests, and failure cases remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report five random view subsets and the same per-scene means and standard deviations in Appendix B. The added experiments introduce no new repeated-run disclosures, uncertainty estimates, or significance tests.

E6.justification: New results concern unordered Diffusion Renderer consistency, its inference time, and downstream reconstruction. Table 5 reports PSNR values of 21.2 and 22.0 dB for guided RGB↔X and Marigold, versus 19.4 and 20.1 for their unguided bases, using method-specific reference predictions. Original Geo-ID benchmark and appendix values are retained.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 newly defines observation weights as geometric confidence multiplied by log(1 + |V(v)|); v1 described their dependence only verbally. This is a limited mathematical specification. The numbered equations, underlying assumptions, and absence of formal proofs otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: training-free geometric consensus improves cross-view consistency while preserving decomposition quality and supporting editable neural scenes.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new downstream test as coherence rather than absolute correctness and attributes Diffusion Renderer’s reconstruction disadvantage to baked-in lighting. Section 4.2 also newly claims the ordered baseline leads only on indoor roughness and metallicity, although Table 1 shows it has lower MAD in all twelve dataset/modality columns. Existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds the explicit observation-weight formula, states that default settings are shared across scenes without per-scene tuning, and supplies a project-page link. These are documentation additions; Appendix A already contained the image resolution, Adam optimizer, and model-specific learning rates in v1.

R1.justification: The same 42 cited works and related-work discussion are retained. Experimental positioning shifts modestly: Diffusion Renderer is explicitly framed as an ordered video upper bound and an unordered competitor, with additional claims about Geo-ID’s runtime and downstream advantages.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized method wording changes, revises consistency and runtime discussion, expands the applications subsection, and adds acknowledgments. The overall section organization and appendix structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 expands Table 1 with an unordered row and revised highlighting, expands Table 4 with a comparator column, and adds downstream Table 5. It also repositions Table 2, restyles Figure 5, and renumbers the retained appendix tables. The original figure content is preserved.

improvement.justification: The matched unordered comparison, quantitative downstream coherence test, and clearer implementation disclosures strengthen the evidence. However, v2 replaces v1’s acknowledgment of the video baseline’s advantage with an inaccurate claim that ordered Diffusion Renderer leads only on indoor roughness and metallicity; Table 1 shows its advantage across all twelve columns. These useful additions and the new error in a central comparative interpretation leave the net quality direction uncertain.
